papers.title: ViT-H: Generative Video-To-Humanoid Control with Motion Tracking Feedback
papers.title_zh: ViT-H: Generative Video-To-Humanoid Control with Motion Tracking Feedback
papers.tldr_zh: Learning humanoid control from monocular human videos offers
papers.cover_zh: Learning humanoid control from monocular human videos offers
papers.abstract_zh: Learning humanoid control from monocular human videos offers a scalable way to acquire diverse whole-body behaviors. Yet, existing reconstruction-retargeting-tracking pipelines are limited in system-level scalability by separately optimized intermediate stages and cannot directly optimize reference motion executability using downstream tracking feedback. We present ViT-H, a video-to-humanoid control framework following a generation-and-tracking paradigm. ViT-H directly generates humanoid reference motions from videos with a diffusion model, bypassing human motion reconstruction and retargeting, and uses motion-tracking outcomes to post-train the generator with direct preference optimization. We further introduce an autoregressive variant that enables real-time humanoid video teleoperation with sub-400 ms latency. Extensive experiments on the Unitree G1 demonstrate that ViT-H outperforms state-of-the-art reconstruction-retargeting-tracking pipelines in both motion quality and executability. We further show that ViT-H scales favorably with model size and with both pre-training and post-training data scale, while motion-tracking feedback consistently improves executability across different motion trackers.

papers.title: DexPort: A Hand-Held Skill Interface for Dexterous Hand Data Collection
papers.title_zh: DexPort：一种用于灵巧手数据收集的手持技能接口
papers.tldr_zh: DexPort手持接口用少量技能收集灵巧手演示，无需机器人即可训练策略。
papers.cover_zh: 不用机器人也能采数据？这个手持接口让灵巧手技能直接复制！
papers.abstract_zh: 收集高质量演示仍然是学习灵巧操作的核心瓶颈。遥操作记录可执行的机器人动作，但需要完整的机器人设置，并将协调多个手指关节的负担放在操作员身上。人类演示更容易收集，但其运动必须被估计并重定向到机器人，且不直接提供机器人动作。在本文中，我们介绍了DexPort，一种用于高自由度机器人手的便携式数据收集接口。它在收集和部署时使用相同的手部硬件，避免了手部具身差距，并记录命令的关节目标和测量的关节状态。我们的关键观察是，少量技能可以支持广泛的灵巧任务。在收集过程中，操作员移动手持接口来指定机器人手腕运动，并选择或调整协调手指运动的技能。这消除了独立控制每个关节的需要，同时保留了精确抓取和手内操作等行为。我们在多个真实世界任务和非结构化环境中收集演示，无需机器人手臂。然后，我们使用行为克隆直接在记录的手腕运动和手部命令上训练视觉运动策略，无需技能标签。我们在4个任务上进行评估：多样物体的拾取和放置、使用手内工具的拧螺丝、需要同时抓取和拉动的抽屉存放，以及双臂扫描任务。我们使用便携式设备在实验室和野外环境中收集了超过2,500个演示。在我们的任务中，使用记录的机器人命令而不是状态时，我们看到了从11%到64%的改进，而使用野外数据时任务成功率从36%到78%的改进。

papers.title: UniAction: Unified Action Conditioning for World Models
papers.title_zh: UniAction：面向世界模型的统一动作条件化框架
papers.tldr_zh: UniAction统一异质动作条件化，联合训练超越专家模型。
papers.cover_zh: 异质动作也能统一建模？联合训练竟反超专家模型！
papers.abstract_zh: 用于条件化世界模型的动作具有高度异质性，因此现有的动作条件化世界模型通常针对单一动作类型构建，导致本就有限的动作标注数据被分散到不同模型中。我们提出 UniAction，一个统一的动作条件化框架，将任意动作表示为稀疏的动作元素集合，每个元素具有离散的语义身份和连续的时空定位坐标。通过将这些坐标直接映射到预训练视频模型的原生位置空间，UniAction 使异质动作能够在相同的时空结构内条件化共享的世界模型。我们进一步引入基数校准注意力，以解决不同动作表示粒度带来的偏差。我们在四种代表性动作形式（力、相机控制、手部姿态和机器人姿态）上评估 UniAction。UniAction 在动作跟随方面优于其他条件化方案，且单一联合训练模型超越了针对特定动作的专家模型，表明异质动作数据受益于统一模型和联合训练。

papers.title: MAST-VLA: Skill-Conditioned Adaptation with Trajectory-Affordance Priors for Multi-Skill Robot Manipulation
papers.title_zh: MAST-VLA: Skill-Conditioned Adaptation with Trajectory-Affordance Priors for Multi-Skill Robot Manipulation
papers.tldr_zh: Generalist robot manipulation requires a single vision-langu
papers.cover_zh: Generalist robot manipulation requires a single vision-langu
papers.abstract_zh: Generalist robot manipulation requires a single vision-language-action (VLA) policy to execute diverse skills across scenes and instructions. However, current multi-skill VLA policies often leave two aspects of an instruction insufficiently modeled: which primitive skill to execute and where/how to contact and move objects. We propose MAST-VLA (Multi-skill Adaptation with Skill-conditioned experts and Trajectory-affordance priors), a dual-conditioning framework for robot manipulation. MAST-VLA introduces skill-conditioned LoRA Mixture-of-Experts (LoRA-MoE) adapters in the LLM backbone, where skill-query tokens and routing biases guide low-rank expert specialization, and converts a predicted affordance heatmap into a patch-level trajectory-affordance spatial prior for the action head. On the CALVIN ABC$→$D long-horizon multi-skill cross-scene generalization setting, MAST-VLA achieves state-of-the-art performance, reaching an Avg. Len of 4.65 over five-subtask evaluation sequences. Real-robot multi-skill sequence experiments further validate its deployability under real perception and control noise.

papers.title: CoCarry: Contact-Support-Structured Retargeting for Dual-Humanoid Cooperative Carrying
papers.title_zh: CoCarry: Contact-Support-Structured Retargeting for Dual-Humanoid Cooperative Carrying
papers.tldr_zh: Recent advances in large-scale human motion data, motion ret
papers.cover_zh: Recent advances in large-scale human motion data, motion ret
papers.abstract_zh: Recent advances in large-scale human motion data, motion retargeting, and motion imitation have enabled increasingly capable whole-body control for individual humanoids. Cooperative carrying is more challenging because successful coordination requires not only plausible individual motions, but also consistent cross-agent and agent-object relations, including shared grasp, relative configuration, and whole-body support. We introduce CoCarry, a cooperative-carrying dataset containing 220 synchronized two-person sequences across 21 task schemes, five shared-object geometries, four terrain types, and approximately 61 minutes of motion. We further propose Contact-Support-Structured Retargeting, which starts from nominal individual motions and jointly refines both humanoids around the same prescribed object trajectory. Cooperation-aware object-local hand anchors preserve compatible four-hand grasp relations, while complementary upper object-interaction and lower support structures retain object-relative geometry and coordinated support. Across all 220 CoCarry sequences retargeted to two A3 humanoids, our method achieves 0.9995 contact preservation, reduces penetration duration by 67.0% and 71.0% relative to GMR and OmniRetarget, respectively, and maintains a 100% retargeting success rate. On CORE4D with Unitree G1 humanoids, it achieves 0.9906 contact preservation with zero measured sliding. We further validate the generated references through physics simulation and multiple real-world cooperative carrying experiments on two physical A3 humanoids, demonstrating their usability for downstream dual-humanoid control.

papers.title: Retiming Robot Demonstrations with a Learned Speed Prior
papers.title_zh: Retiming Robot Demonstrations with a Learned Speed Prior
papers.tldr_zh: The pace of a robot demonstration is often determined by the
papers.cover_zh: The pace of a robot demonstration is often determined by the
papers.abstract_zh: The pace of a robot demonstration is often determined by the teleoperator rather than by the task itself. As a result, the same motion can appear at widely different speeds across demonstrations, and policies trained on such data may inherit operator-specific timing along with task behavior. We propose to learn a speed prior directly from large-scale demonstration data. Given a task instruction, a motion path and the images along it, it predicts a distribution over execution speed along the path, from which a chosen quantile defines a consistent clock for retiming each demonstration. Existing methods derive the acceleration signal from the very data they accelerate, so each new task costs another fit, annotation, or pair of predefined rates. A single trained speed prior instead covers every task in a corpus. We fit a speed prior on both robot teleoperation data and handheld demonstrations in which a human arm, rather than a robot arm, moves the gripper, and use it to retime robot demonstrations to the handheld pace before fine-tuning a vision-language-action policy. For execution, we pair the policy with a real-time optimal-control layer that tracks predicted action chunks under robot constraints using the predicted pace. On 120 RoboLab tasks, policies fine-tuned on our learned clocks succeed more often and move with up to half the jerk compared with policies fine-tuned on the original demonstration timing and uniformly accelerated to the same speed. On a real robot, our policy stacks cups in 3.50s, 1.72$×$ faster than the default policy's 6.02s while succeeding as often, in 29 of 30 trials. Videos and further material are available at https://mllab.snu.ac.kr/projects/learned_speed_prior.

papers.title: Do VLAs Know They Will Fail? Interpretable Success and Failure Patterns in Physical AI Systems
papers.title_zh: Do VLAs Know They Will Fail? Interpretable Success and Failure Patterns in Physical AI Systems
papers.tldr_zh: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as powerful
papers.cover_zh: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as powerful
papers.abstract_zh: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as powerful general-purpose robot policies, but their successes and failures remain difficult to diagnose and understand. In this work, we show that sparse autoencoder (SAE) representations of OpenVLA activations contain outcome-predictive information and can be used to predict task failure before the robot reaches an unrecoverable state. Moreover, to provide insights into what common behaviors may contribute to these outcomes, we identify individual SAE features whose strong activations are associated with specific stages of success or failure, and uncover recurring behavioral patterns by localizing temporal intervals where these features exhibit significant activation changes. We further develop a VLM-based interpretation pipeline to generate behavioral descriptions of these patterns and validate their correspondence to feature activations on held-out intervals.

papers.title: From Tabletop to Walking Bot: Deploying a VLA Model on a Legged Manipulator Robot
papers.title_zh: From Tabletop to Walking Bot: Deploying a VLA Model on a Legged Manipulator Robot
papers.tldr_zh: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are typically pretrained
papers.cover_zh: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are typically pretrained
papers.abstract_zh: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are typically pretrained on broad, diverse datasets and subsequently fine-tuned on a comparatively small dataset tailored to a specific target robot. Such adaptation recipe is now widely established, achieving its most mature results on fixed-base arms due to their static base dynamics and consistent reference frame. Mounting the same arm on a quadruped extends the workspace to the entire floor, but fundamentally changes the embodiment: rather than controlling the arm in isolation, the policy must jointly coordinate base navigation, body posture, and end-effector motion. In this work, we study the practical demands of this embodiment change across data collection, model adaptation, and inference design to achieve closed-loop loco-manipulation on a Unitree Go2 with an AgileX Piper arm. We report the choices that made this real-robot deployment feasible, namely model variant, action horizon, and demonstration conventions, together with a study tailored to a pick-and-place task, separating data coverage from model capacity. We show that expanding demonstration coverage reduces held-out end-effector error by 30%, and incorporating secondary skills (such as pushing rather than grasping) introduces new behavioral modes without degrading baseline performance. Finally, closed-loop real-world experiments show how dataset composition shapes success and failure, validating the pipeline for more complex loco-manipulation.

papers.title: When Does Dynamics Randomization Test Context Inference?
papers.title_zh: When Does Dynamics Randomization Test Context Inference?
papers.tldr_zh: Environments with randomized dynamics are widely used to ask
papers.cover_zh: Environments with randomized dynamics are widely used to ask
papers.abstract_zh: Environments with randomized dynamics are widely used to ask whether world models need explicit context inference. However, randomization can leave little predictive information for a context encoder to add, because distinct latent parameters may produce similar transitions at visited states, or those states may already reveal the active context. We formalize the remaining one-step information as predictive headroom and compare kernels under fixed and visited state--action distributions to distinguish changes in query coverage from changes in context weights. We analyze discrete and continuous environments and find low headroom both when kernels differ little and when visitation reduces an otherwise large discrepancy. At the same time, resetting state components increases headroom, showing that context evidence accumulates in state. We propose reporting this headroom alongside the randomized parameters, so that gains from explicit context inference can be interpreted relative to the information missing from the current state and action.

papers.title: MDMR-Bench: A Multi-Dimensional Benchmark for Multi-Reference Image Generation
papers.title_zh: MDMR-Bench: A Multi-Dimensional Benchmark for Multi-Reference Image Generation
papers.tldr_zh: Image generation models have rapidly advanced, with many mod
papers.cover_zh: Image generation models have rapidly advanced, with many mod
papers.abstract_zh: Image generation models have rapidly advanced, with many models now supporting generation conditioned on multiple reference images and textual instructions. Such models enable a wide range of applications, including entity fusion and attribute transfer across images. However, existing benchmarks for multi-reference image generation rely on limited evaluation dimensions and fail to capture the diverse challenges of the task. To address this limitation, we propose MDMR-Bench, a Multi-Dimensional benchmark for Multi-Reference image generation. MDMR-Bench is organized around representative capability settings and consists of multiple evaluation subsets spanning diverse dimensions of multi-reference image generation, including (1) common entity fusion and attribute transfer, (2) multi-element extraction from a single image, (3) infographic manipulation, and (4) visual reasoning-intensive generation. This design enables systematic analysis of model capabilities and failure modes across different challenge dimensions. Furthermore, to achieve more reliable and interpretable evaluation, we introduce a checklist-based evaluation protocol that decomposes generation quality into fine-grained evaluation aspects. Instead of relying solely on holistic scoring, our framework uses structured checklists composed of both global-level and atomic-level queries, enabling more diagnostic assessment of model performance. By benchmarking both open-source and proprietary models, we demonstrate that MDMR-Bench provides fine-grained insights into model performance across different dimensions. The dataset and code are publicly available.

papers.title: When Human Corrections Travel: Safety in Federated VLA Adaptation
papers.title_zh: When Human Corrections Travel: Safety in Federated VLA Adaptation
papers.tldr_zh: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies can adapt to local hum
papers.cover_zh: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies can adapt to local hum
papers.abstract_zh: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies can adapt to local human intervention, while federated learning can combine distributed robot experience without pooling raw records. We examine their prospective intersection: sharing adaptations derived from diverse human corrections across tasks, environments, people, and robot embodiments. Corrections differ in modality, safety semantics(urgency, behavioral scope, etc.), and privacy sensitivity. A shared update that improves mean task success may suppress a rare safety intervention or produce an unsafe response on another robot. We argue for three requirements: preserve the context and uncertainty of multimodal corrections when deciding what to share; assess candidate updates in each receiving robot's closed loop before deployment; and evaluate leakage alongside retention of safety-critical evidence. Immediate, legible defensive behavior remains necessary during human interaction. We offer counterexamples and a falsifiable evaluation agenda, not experimental results.

papers.title: DT-JEPA: Learning to Predict Future Representations for Decision-Making
papers.title_zh: DT-JEPA: Learning to Predict Future Representations for Decision-Making
papers.tldr_zh: Decision Transformer (DT) has demonstrated strong performanc
papers.cover_zh: Decision Transformer (DT) has demonstrated strong performanc
papers.abstract_zh: Decision Transformer (DT) has demonstrated strong performance in various offline reinforcement learning (RL) tasks by conditioning action generation on expected future returns and historical trajectories. However, treating expected future returns as the condition provides an incomplete description of the future, as trajectories with different state transitions and behaviors may share similar returns. Moreover, expected future returns inherently depend on task-specific reward functions, which makes policy learning reliant on reward-labeled datasets and restricts its scalability to tasks with similar but unseen rewards. Recently, Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPA) have emerged as a promising paradigm of self-supervised learning-based world models, which learn predictive representations of future dynamics in latent space rather than reconstructing future states in the original space. Inspired by JEPA, we propose DT-JEPA, an offline pretraining and online fine-tuning framework that learns general knowledge from reward-free offline trajectories and achieves excellent adaptation to unseen tasks. Instead of predicting a single deterministic future embedding, we design a novel probabilistic predictor to model the conditional distribution of future representations in the latent space, thereby capturing both predictive information and uncertainty about future dynamics. Theoretically, we show that 1) the JEPA objective seeks to maximize a variational lower bound on the mutual information between historical representations and future trajectories; and 2) predictive future-conditioned policy learning admits a finite-sample performance bound with an O(N-1/4) estimation term. Experiments on D4RL benchmarks demonstrate that DT-JEPA achieves efficient adaptation across varying offline RL tasks, outperforming traditional DT-based and other offline RL methods.

papers.title: Delay Randomization Widens the Delay Margin of Learned Humanoid Motion Trackers
papers.title_zh: Delay Randomization Widens the Delay Margin of Learned Humanoid Motion Trackers
papers.tldr_zh: Learned humanoid controllers are usually trained in one simu
papers.cover_zh: Learned humanoid controllers are usually trained in one simu
papers.abstract_zh: Learned humanoid controllers are usually trained in one simulator and then checked in a second one before they go near hardware. We ask what that check says about command delay. We train motion-tracking policies for a 24-joint humanoid on five motions taken from monocular video and test them in an independent CPU MuJoCo harness, which we first verify against the training model. Every policy completes its motion in at least 26 of 30 episodes under the training randomization. With 40 ms of constant command delay, however, survival drops to 15% on average (0% - 45%), and the delay margin is only 20 - 30 ms. Randomizing the delay during training (0 - 50 ms) lifts survival at 40 ms to 95% on average (75% - 100%) and moves the margin to 50 - 70 ms. A control arm trained for the same number of extra iterations without delay does not improve, so the gain comes from the randomization itself. This holds for all five motions with three training seeds each, and a policy trained in PhysX behaves the same way. The price is slightly looser tracking (0.02 - 0.06 rad on four motions) and, for the most dynamic motion, less robustness to other perturbations. We also show that the first sim-to-sim gap we saw came from the harness, a missing floor and a wrong timestep, and not from the physics engines. The 0 - 20 ms delay ranges common in locomotion training lie inside the margin an unrandomized tracker already has. The benefit comes from randomizing beyond it, so the range should be set from the robot's measured latency, and delay margin belongs next to other sim-to-sim metrics.

papers.title: HGWM: Hierarchical Graph-Guided World Model for Zero-Shot Object Navigation via Graph Matching
papers.title_zh: HGWM: Hierarchical Graph-Guided World Model for Zero-Shot Object Navigation via Graph Matching
papers.tldr_zh: Zero-shot object navigation requires an embodied agent to ch
papers.cover_zh: Zero-shot object navigation requires an embodied agent to ch
papers.abstract_zh: Zero-shot object navigation requires an embodied agent to choose where to search while retaining evidence from previous observations. HGWM couples an LLM-generated room-anchor prior with persistent spatial-semantic memory. A coarse stage assigns visual-semantic scores to candidate headings on a 0-10 scale; a fine stage measures symbolic compatibility between observed objects, room context, and the goal prior. Phase-dependent fusion combines these scores with an LLM direction recommendation before local action selection. On HM3D v0.1, the reported HGWM configuration achieves 62.6% success rate (SR) and 31.5% success weighted by path length (SPL), compared with 58.1% and 31.2% for WMNav. On MP3D, the corresponding values are 46.8% and 17.9%, compared with 45.4% and 17.2%. The results indicate higher success point estimates and modest path-efficiency gains. On HM3D v0.2, the full model obtains 74.4% SR and 31.9% SPL. Additional component ablations reduce SR by 0.9-2.3 percentage points and SPL by 0.6-1.5 points. These are author-reported aggregate measurements. The accompanying implementation repairs pass offline tests; episode-level rerun records are not available. Evaluation is confined to simulation.

papers.title: Predictive Long-Horizon Progress Modeling with Action-Aware Quantification
papers.title_zh: Predictive Long-Horizon Progress Modeling with Action-Aware Quantification
papers.tldr_zh: Quantitative and dense task progress feedback is essential f
papers.cover_zh: Quantitative and dense task progress feedback is essential f
papers.abstract_zh: Quantitative and dense task progress feedback is essential for robotic manipulation across data curation, policy evaluation, and reinforcement learning. Existing progress annotations often rely on sparse keyframe markings derived from subjective manual judgments, limiting their scalability and cross-task consistency, particularly in long-horizon manipulation. To overcome these challenges, we propose action-aware quantification, a unified progress specification that decomposes long-horizon trajectories into object-level subtasks via a vision-language model (VLM) and assigns weighted action credits to capture fine-grained execution dynamics. Using VLM auto-labeling and human calibration, we construct an 800+ hour training video dataset and LOOM, a long-horizon progress benchmark containing 19,618 human-calibrated evaluation frames. To model these dense progress dynamics, we introduce NimCritic, a predictive progress critic trained via Joint Video-Progress Learning. We further incorporate Historical Progress Perturbation to mitigate sequential drift, and design a contrastive Video-Progress Alignment objective that bridges asymmetric expert streams by mutually grounding intermediate visual dynamics and denoised progress trajectories. NimCritic matches or outperforms state-of-the-art process reward models (PRMs) on the established Video Progress Benchmark (VPB) and LOOM, surpassing GVL (GPT-6-Sol) on VPB by about 65% in terminal success accuracy (TSA). On the large-scale RoboArena policy evaluation benchmark, it also retrieves human-selected successful rollouts with about 97% overall recall. These results establish action-aware quantification as a scalable foundation for dense progress feedback in robotic manipulation.

papers.cover_zh: We introduce RynnUnify, a 16B unified embodied model that co
papers.abstract_zh: We introduce RynnUnify, a 16B unified embodied model that combines strong embodied understanding with long-horizon visual planning through interleaved video--language reasoning. With capabilities spanning spatial reasoning, physical prediction, and grounding, RynnUnify connects an understanding of the physical world with visual anticipation of how it evolves across successive subtasks. Building on these capabilities, we further develop an agentic extension through reinforcement learning to selectively use video predictions for reasoning about unobserved states and interaction outcomes. We also develop a world-action extension of the full RynnUnify model, translating its understanding and prediction capabilities into robot control. To evaluate these capabilities, we introduce Rynn-VP and Rynn-GEU for long-horizon visual planning and anticipatory reasoning. Experiments show that RynnUnify achieves the highest average embodied understanding score among the evaluated unified multimodal models and improves the Rynn-VP overall score by 9.75 points over Cosmos 3 Nano. Its agentic extension improves the Rynn-GEU average by 6.0 points over direct reasoning, while the world-action extension achieves 51.5\% success on 20 selected composite RoboCasa365 tasks and 46.7\% average success across three real-robot tasks. Together, these results establish RynnUnify as a shared foundation for embodied understanding, visual planning, and robot control, taking a step toward a unified embodied brain.

papers.title: RobustRLlib: A Unified Library and Benchmark for Robust Reinforcement Learning Algorithms
papers.title_zh: RobustRLlib：面向鲁棒强化学习算法的统一库与基准
papers.tldr_zh: RobustRLlib统一17种鲁棒RL算法，提供基准评估能力边界。
papers.cover_zh: 鲁棒RL算法大乱斗｜这个库一次集齐17种，还告诉你谁更强
papers.abstract_zh: 鲁棒强化学习（RL）对于可靠的实际部署至关重要，因为策略可能在各种变化和干扰下失效。现有的鲁棒RL算法提供了丰富的机制和原则，但两个主要障碍限制了它们更广泛的潜力：算法可重用性有限，以及经验能力边界不清晰。我们推出了RobustRLlib，一个以算法为中心的库和基准，旨在解决这两个挑战。它在统一接口下集成了17种代表性的鲁棒在线、离线和安全RL算法，显著提高了可重用性，并提供了一个增强的评估平台，涵盖多样化的现实世界变化以及先进的类人机器人和视觉-语言-动作任务。通过对273种扰动配置的系统评估，我们提供了当前鲁棒RL算法的最新能力图谱，揭示了它们仍然有效的领域以及持续存在重大鲁棒性差距的地方。作为一个开源、用户友好的平台，RobustRLlib提供了一个可复现且可扩展的代码库，用于将现有方法应用于新问题并开发新的鲁棒RL算法。

papers.title: SceneBloom: Agentic Indoor Environment Generation with Realistic and Diverse Layouts for Embodied Learning
papers.title_zh: SceneBloom：面向具身学习的逼真多样布局的智能体室内环境生成
papers.tldr_zh: SceneBloom智能体框架生成逼真室内布局，无碰撞且提升导航策略泛化。
papers.cover_zh: 终于不用手工搭场景｜这个智能体框架让仿真环境直接可用
papers.abstract_zh: 训练可泛化的具身智能体需要逼真、多样且可直接用于仿真的室内环境。语言引导方法支持语义规划和物体级推理，但精确的空间定位仍然困难。视觉生成模型提供了关于合理布局的丰富先验，但其输出需要几何推理才能成为物理有效的3D场景。我们提出SceneBloom，一个智能体框架，将视觉布局采样与契约引导的3D编译相结合。分层采样器利用扩散先验在功能区内生成家具布局。编译器则利用从每个提案中提取的关系来指导几何拟合和局部姿态校正。在五种房间类型上，SceneBloom在比较方法中获得了最高的视觉质量和物理稳定性，并且是唯一没有检测到网格碰撞和越界物体的方法。其布局也比所有比较基线更接近真实房间的分布。在这些逼真场景中训练的物体导航策略在留出的真实扫描数据上比在等量真实训练扫描上训练的策略取得了更高的成功率。代码见 https://github.com/Tinaliu0123/scenebloom。

papers.title: If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs
papers.title_zh: If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs
papers.tldr_zh: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models perform well on robotic
papers.cover_zh: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models perform well on robotic
papers.abstract_zh: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models perform well on robotic manipulation, yet remain brittle once their own actions carry them into states their training data barely covers. Recovering from such failures usually requires recovery demonstrations, policy retraining, or a separate model at inference time. We introduce Backtrack, a lightweight failure detection and recovery mechanism for frozen VLAs that needs none of these. A small failure prediction head, trained only on outcome-labeled rollouts of the frozen policy, reads the VLA's existing internal representations to estimate whether the current episode will fail. When the predicted failure probability exceeds a threshold, a controller pauses the policy, retraces the arm's recently achieved motion, and hands control back to the unchanged policy so it can retry from an earlier configuration. The head adds only 0.48-0.88% to the policy's parameter count. We evaluate Backtrack on LIBERO with three VLAs spanning two action-generation families: SmolVLA and $π$0.5, which use flow-matching action experts, and the autoregressive $π$0-FAST. On LIBERO-Long, the suite of long-horizon multi-step tasks and the one on which all three policies fail most often, Backtrack reduces each policy's failure rate by 19-48%, raising success by up to 7.4 percentage points; on the three shorter suites, where control success is already 85-99%, its effect is smaller. On MetaWorld, all twelve controller configurations tested with SmolVLA improve on the unassisted policy.

papers.title: RoboCode: Learning Reusable Action Primitives for Robot Manipulation
papers.title_zh: RoboCode: Learning Reusable Action Primitives for Robot Manipulation
papers.tldr_zh: Recent robot manipulation policies commonly predict continuo
papers.cover_zh: Recent robot manipulation policies commonly predict continuo
papers.abstract_zh: Recent robot manipulation policies commonly predict continuous action chunks directly from observations, without explicitly modeling reusable structure in the action space. However, manipulation demonstrations often contain recurring short-horizon motion patterns that are shared across tasks. We introduce textsc{RoboCode}, which learns these patterns through a shared soft-gated primitive action interface. Rather than assigning each action chunk to a single discrete code, textsc{RoboCode} represents it as a soft composition of multiple learned primitives, providing a flexible intermediate representation of short-horizon actions. The primitive interface is learned from action chunks pooled across multiple tasks and then frozen while task-specific state encoders are trained to map current state inputs into the shared latent space. Experiments on five ManiSkill manipulation tasks address three questions. First, the learned primitive interface reconstructs action chunks with an average reconstruction MSE of 0.0187. Second, analysis of code activations reveals structured code reuse across tasks. Third, textsc{RoboCode} achieves the highest or tied closed-loop success rate on all evaluated tasks, with an average success rate of 75.6%, compared with 68.8% for ACT and 41.6% for the larger Diffusion Policy baseline. These results suggest that soft-gated primitive codebooks provide an effective and interpretable intermediate action representation for robot manipulation.

papers.title: Regularised RL improves sim-to-real transfer
papers.title_zh: Regularised RL improves sim-to-real transfer
papers.tldr_zh: Regularised reinforcement learning (RL) has provable robustn
papers.cover_zh: Regularised reinforcement learning (RL) has provable robustn
papers.abstract_zh: Regularised reinforcement learning (RL) has provable robustness guarantees that should ease the transfer of policies from simulation to robots, known as sim-to-real. Yet, weakly regularised algorithms like Proximal Policy Optimisation (PPO) remain the de facto choice in sim-to-real pipelines, while the practical benefits of regularisation for transfer remain poorly characterised. In this work, we study the sim-to-real performance of commonly used RL algorithms, with the aim of characterising the effects of regularisation on robotic performance. To that end, we derive Soft MellowMax Actor-Critic (SMM-AC), a novel regularised RL algorithm based on the soft mellowmax value function, which carries strong robustness guarantees. On MuJoCo continuous control benchmarks, SMM-AC is competitive with baselines like Soft Actor-Critic (SAC). On real robots, SMM-AC achieves higher return, while exhibiting greater robustness to perturbations in observations, the environment, and dynamics than baselines. Together, these results demonstrate that regularised RL improves real-world policy deployment through better robustness to the sim-to-real gap, and changing real-world conditions.

papers.title: HoloBoxing: A Simple Recipe for Humanoid Boxing with 7 Minutes of Single-GPU Training
papers.title_zh: HoloBoxing: A Simple Recipe for Humanoid Boxing with 7 Minutes of Single-GPU Training
papers.tldr_zh: HoloBoxing presents a simple recipe for learning humanoid bo
papers.cover_zh: HoloBoxing presents a simple recipe for learning humanoid bo
papers.abstract_zh: HoloBoxing presents a simple recipe for learning humanoid boxing by building on a pretrained whole-body controller. The recipe separates reusable motor skills from task decisions: a compact planner requests future body-point targets, while the frozen controller handles joint-level execution. A learned decoder maps 32-dimensional actions to structured target windows, and measured-state imitation initializes the planner before reinforcement learning. Task learning then refines interaction behavior while reusing the decoder and controller, avoiding the need to relearn whole-body control. This combination keeps task optimization focused on a compact upper policy and supplies an initial behavior before reward-driven exploration. Starting from that available controller, the recipe accounts for about seven minutes of additional training, including reused representation fitting and a single-GPU task run. This excludes controller pretraining, data preparation, evaluation, and search. Simulated boxing experiments and component controls evaluate the resulting behavior and the roles of imitation initialization and the target representation.

papers.title: SKG in Practice: OOD Generalization Cases Across FourDomains
papers.title_zh: SKG in Practice: OOD Generalization Cases Across FourDomains
papers.tldr_zh: This paper presents the engineering implementation methods o
papers.cover_zh: This paper presents the engineering implementation methods o
papers.abstract_zh: This paper presents the engineering implementation methods of the SKG inference framework and provides complete case studies across four domains. Case 1, 2D Dissipative Mechanical System: OOD MSE is 1.69 to 4.12 times lower than the best neural baseline; the state-dependent metric yields a 10^8-order improvement under controlled conditions. Case 2, Target Detection Sim-to-Real: Real-machine mAP increases from 0.2564 to 0.4964 (+24.00 points, single-run experiment, 32 images, point estimate), and AP75 increases from 0.1736 to 0.5765 (+40.29 points), with no real-machine retraining required. Case 3, Sequence Modeling sine to square: OOD MSE is 0.0296 versus Transformer 0.0641 (mean of 5 seeds, p=0.024). Case 4, Molecular Dynamics MD17: ID@100 ADE is 0.0285 versus ESTAG 0.1467; OOD@100 is 0.0316 versus 0.1411 (single seed). For each case, we present the objective, applied SKG theory, parameter settings, baseline comparison protocol, data results, and sources of advantage. Following the cases, we provide the complete methodology: pre-validation, task invariant construction, three-stage training, residual training, and the four theorems and one proposition supporting these methods. This paper not only demonstrates effective configurations of SKG across four domains but also honestly reports the variance of single-run experiments, limitations of single-seed results, negative updates caused by parameterization mismatch, and practical experience of using engineering thresholds as diagnostic signals rather than hard constraints.

papers.title: DynaSlots: Slot-Centric 3D Dynamics Pretraining for Robot Manipulation
papers.title_zh: DynaSlots: Slot-Centric 3D Dynamics Pretraining for Robot Manipulation
papers.tldr_zh: Robot manipulation involves localized changes: picking up a
papers.cover_zh: Robot manipulation involves localized changes: picking up a
papers.abstract_zh: Robot manipulation involves localized changes: picking up a cup moves the cup while leaving the surrounding scene largely unchanged. Yet existing 3D visual pretraining methods, including recent dynamics-aware variants, model state transitions at the scene level, compressing the motion of everything in a scene into a single global latent action. This conflates semantically distinct transitions in scenes with multiple moving parts, obscures dependencies between changing regions, and leaves the learned representation vulnerable to task-irrelevant scene content. We introduce DynaSlots, an action-free, label-free pretraining framework that decomposes each point cloud frame into a small set of temporally consistent slots and models dynamics at this per-slot level rather than the scene level. A temporal slot propagation module promotes consistent slot assignments across frames; an inverse dynamics model then extracts one latent action per slot from feature differences, and a diffusion-based forward dynamics model, paired with a self-supervised interaction head, predicts each slot's future state while learning pairwise proximity-and-motion relations. Experiments on Meta-World, Adroit, and a RealMan RM65-B robot demonstrate that DynaSlots outperforms prior scene-level baselines. It achieves superior success rates in simulation and exhibits strong robustness to scene clutter and unseen objects in real-world manipulation. Code is available at href{https://zhucezhanghao12345-source.github.io/DynaSlots-Anonymous/}{https://zhucezhanghao12345-source.github.io/DynaSlots-Anonymous/}.

papers.title: LogLook: Execution-Grounded Memory for Frontier-Model Robot Planners
papers.title_zh: LogLook: Execution-Grounded Memory for Frontier-Model Robot Planners
papers.tldr_zh: Many manipulation tasks require a robot to remember what it
papers.cover_zh: Many manipulation tasks require a robot to remember what it
papers.abstract_zh: Many manipulation tasks require a robot to remember what it has done and what it has seen. Frontier vision-language models can plan such tasks without task-specific training, but how such a planner should remember an episode is an open question. We argue that its memory must keep track of what the planner has done and learned, and must let the planner choose what to look at, since every frame costs tokens; a note rewritten at every step meets both poorly. We propose LogLook, whose execution-grounded memory lets the system keep the record, an execution log and the model's earlier notes, while the model decides where to look: frames are returned only where it expects a change, and demonstrations are skimmed before it inspects the parts it chooses. Measured with the benchmark's motion planner, LogLook matches the success of a note-only memory with 43% fewer tokens and less than half the images, and fails far fewer episodes through what it remembered or saw. With direct control, LogLook solves 93.5% of the RoboMME test set.

papers.title: VERA-Hand: A Verified Multidimensional Benchmark for 2D Hand Pose Estimation in Third-Person Dynamic Gesture Videos
papers.title_zh: VERA-Hand: A Verified Multidimensional Benchmark for 2D Hand Pose Estimation in Third-Person Dynamic Gesture Videos
papers.tldr_zh: Hand landmarks serve as input for gesture recognition, sign
papers.cover_zh: Hand landmarks serve as input for gesture recognition, sign
papers.abstract_zh: Hand landmarks serve as input for gesture recognition, sign language understanding, and touchless human-computer interaction. Yet hand pose estimators are typically evaluated with frame-wise localization metrics such as PCK or MPJPE, which are computed over matched predictions and overlook missed or spurious hands, handedness errors, and temporal instability. To address these limitations, we present VERA-Hand, a benchmark that evaluates estimators using manually verified, frame-level 2D annotations for 10,690 hands across four complementary dimensions (detection, localization, identification, and temporal stability), as well as a joint Pose-F1 metric that requires both correct detection and accurate localization. Evaluating six estimators spanning hand-specific, whole-body, reconstruction-based, and foundation-model paradigms, we find that no estimator dominates: rankings reorder sharply across dimensions. VERA-Hand also exposes failures that localization-only and downstream evaluations may not reveal, including cross-hand overlap in over 85% of frames for a recent foundation model. A post-hoc cleanup case study demonstrates how the benchmark can validate corrective interventions, while stratified analyses show that robustness varies across motion-blur classes and hand regions. We release the verified annotations, protocol, and code at https://gibranbenitez.github.io/VERA_Hand/

papers.title: From Freehand Demonstrations to Autonomous Robotic Ultrasound: An Anatomy-Anchored Learning Framework
papers.title_zh: From Freehand Demonstrations to Autonomous Robotic Ultrasound: An Anatomy-Anchored Learning Framework
papers.tldr_zh: Ultrasound imaging is highly operator-dependent, motivating
papers.cover_zh: Ultrasound imaging is highly operator-dependent, motivating
papers.abstract_zh: Ultrasound imaging is highly operator-dependent, motivating robotic systems that reproduce expert scanning skills consistently. These skills involve coordinated interpretation of anatomical landmarks, ultrasound images, and probe-tissue interactions that are difficult to encode in hand-designed control strategies. Imitation learning offers an alternative, but its observation and action representations should reflect the anatomically structured nature of scanning. We propose an anatomy-anchored imitation-learning framework that combines anatomy-guided probe placement with learned ultrasound navigation. The placement module identifies a task-specific anatomical starting point from external visual observations and establishes the initial probe pose as the reference frame for scanning. A flow-based policy then generates scanning motions from anchor-relative probe poses, ultrasound images, probe-mounted camera views, and contact forces, while a termination head predicts task completion. This avoids continuous reliance on third-person vision and reduces dependence on the robot-patient configuration. A handheld acquisition platform enables multimodal demonstrations to be collected during natural freehand scanning without a robot. On 16 unseen participants, task success reaches 96%, 94%, 88%, and 94% for kidney, gallbladder, and liver standard-plane acquisition and radial artery sweeping, respectively. Compared with a fine-tuned pi_0 model, success on the abdominal tasks improves by 10-42 percentage points, with lower time-to-target, peak contact force, and trajectory jerk. Ablations support the complementary roles of anatomical anchoring, egocentric vision, and force feedback. End-to-end trials with automatic placement achieve 90-100% success, and the policies transfer without retraining to a second robot with 83-100% success.

papers.title: Adaptive World-Models for Anomaly Recognition (AWARE): A Framework for Robot Dynamics Prediction and Introspection
papers.title_zh: Adaptive World-Models for Anomaly Recognition (AWARE): A Framework for Robot Dynamics Prediction and Introspection
papers.tldr_zh: Unrecognized anomalies in critical infrastructure can rapidl
papers.cover_zh: Unrecognized anomalies in critical infrastructure can rapidl
papers.abstract_zh: Unrecognized anomalies in critical infrastructure can rapidly cascade into catastrophic physical or operational failures. Current anomaly detection approaches often rely on direct access to the monitored system by utilizing onboard sensors, such as motor encoders, to detect anomalous states. However, legacy hardware often lacks these sensors, or strict security protocols may prohibit access altogether. We therefore present AWARE, a world model framework that is capable of anomaly detection using only external camera monitoring via system dynamics estimation and state prediction. Evaluated across 240 real-world robotic crane trajectories, including payload collisions and motor degradations, AWARE demonstrates a 26% improvement in anomaly classification over our strongest baseline under noisy, camera-only state estimation. Furthermore, the inferred dynamics parameter can be decoded to identify the source of faults, localizing the degrading motor with 88% accuracy.

papers.title: ZENO: Nonlinear filtering with Zakai Equation Neural Operators
papers.title_zh: ZENO: Nonlinear filtering with Zakai Equation Neural Operators
papers.tldr_zh: State inference and parameter learning for nonlinear filters
papers.cover_zh: State inference and parameter learning for nonlinear filters
papers.abstract_zh: State inference and parameter learning for nonlinear filters is a core computation for scientific machine learning with varied applications in engineering and neuroscience. The unnormalized filtering distribution is governed by the Zakai equation, a stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE) that combines the forward Kolmogorov operator (known as the Fokker-Planck equation) with observed likelihood updates. Although solving these high-dimensional SPDEs is often impossible analytically and intractable numerically, advances in operator learning and physics-informed machine learning have made it feasible. Harnessing these advances, we introduce the Zakai Equation Neural Operator (ZENO), a model that optimizes a neural operator against a Zakai Equation based physics-informed loss to approximate the exact unnormalized filtering distribution for latent stochastic dynamical systems. We use this ZENO-inferred posterior distribution in an expectation-maximization (EM) framework to perform parameter learning and state inference. We demonstrate ZENO's ability to accurately infer the posterior distribution and learn its corresponding SDE parameters in three simulated stochastic dynamical systems (Double-Well bistable system, Van Der Pol (VDP) oscillator, and Lorenz system) and compare its performance against established methods for latent SDE inference and learning. We show that ZENO recovers previously observed limit cycles representing forward and backward locomotion from a whole-brain imaging dataset of immobilized textit{C. elegans} nematodes. ZENO is a novel approach to the problem of nonlinear filtering and dynamical inference through the lens of partial differential equations and operator theory.

papers.title: Robotic Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided Geometric Modeling of Soft Tissue: 3D Representations for Data-Driven Closed-Loop Shape Control
papers.title_zh: Robotic Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided Geometric Modeling of Soft Tissue: 3D Representations for Data-Driven Closed-Loop Shape Control
papers.tldr_zh: In medical robotics, data-driven soft-tissue shape control r
papers.cover_zh: In medical robotics, data-driven soft-tissue shape control r
papers.abstract_zh: In medical robotics, data-driven soft-tissue shape control requires deforming tissue toward desired morphologies through sequential physical interactions. This challenge is particularly important in microscale manipulation, where localized deformation is difficult to observe, represent, and control, while physics-based models can be computationally expensive and difficult to adapt to realistic environments. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) provides high-resolution volumetric perception of tissue deformation, but target-conditioned control requires effective representations of both observed and desired tissue states. In this work, we introduce an OCT-guided data-driven framework for tissue shape control, learned from user-guided demonstrations and executed with closed-loop OCT feedback. We study full-volume, tissue-masked sparse-volume, and voxelized point-cloud representations, with or without residual conditioning, using deterministic (Explicit) and generative diffusion (Diffusion) policies. Across 12 configurations and 576 phantom rollouts on 3-DoF depth and 6-DoF directional tasks, OCT-derived 3D representations support both Explicit and Diffusion policies, with performance depending on representation and residual conditioning. Residual conditioning reduces directional Shape RMSE from 0.748 to 0.555 mm for full-volume Diffusion, while voxelized point-cloud Explicit with residuals achieves 0.534 mm for depth and 0.443 mm for directional control, with comparable accuracy at intermediate unseen targets and consistent performance across deployments. We further evaluate the framework in 60 ex vivo porcine rollouts, extending to biological tissue with final geometric errors comparable to human demonstrations. These results establish volumetric OCT as current and goal representations for learned closed-loop tissue shape control across deterministic and generative action models.

papers.title: MiD-VLM: Detecting and Grounding Global Semantic Misinformation in Image-Caption Pairs
papers.title_zh: MiD-VLM: Detecting and Grounding Global Semantic Misinformation in Image-Caption Pairs
papers.tldr_zh: Semantic misinformation can arise when an authentic image is
papers.cover_zh: Semantic misinformation can arise when an authentic image is
papers.abstract_zh: Semantic misinformation can arise when an authentic image is paired with a caption that changes or distorts its narrative. Because the image itself may contain no visible signs of manipulation, methods designed to detect pixel-level artifacts can miss these misleading image-caption pairs. We study this problem using DGM4+, a dataset designed to evaluate the detection of global scene and semantic inconsistencies. We propose a multimodal model that combines image-text representations from SigLIP with visual scene features from DINOv2 through a projection MLP, and adapts Qwen2-VL-7B using LoRA. The model jointly predicts whether an image-caption pair is authentic, identifies the manipulation type, and grounds the misleading caption tokens. On the DGM4+ validation split, the model achieves an F1 score of $0.9679$ for binary authenticity classification. These results suggest that parameter-efficient adaptation of vision-language models is promising for detecting semantic inconsistencies, while also motivating further work on precise token-level grounding.
